backlog.title: F15 — Community Package-Manager Distribution
backlog.description: Publish every QMKonnect release to native package/version managers users already trust: AUR and Nix flake (Linux), Homebrew (macOS), Scoop and Winget (Windows), plus cross-platform mise/asdf plugins. Each channel honors the per-user, no-admin philosophy where the channel permits. F1-F14 are already fully implemented in the v0.2.8 codebase (390 tests passing); this phase closes the last PRD feature gap (F15).

milestones.title: Linux Community Channels (AUR + Nix)
milestones.description: Create the AUR binary package (qmkonnect-bin) that downloads GitHub release artifacts instead of building from source, and a Nix flake that builds from source with proper Linux dependency integration. Both must install the udev rule, hid-id helper, and systemd service template.

tasks.title: AUR Binary Package (qmkonnect-bin)
tasks.description: Create an AUR `-bin` package that fetches pre-built release artifacts from GitHub instead of building from source. The existing `packaging/linux/arch/PKGBUILD` is a source-build for local makepkg; the AUR package needs a separate PKGBUILD pointing at release tarballs with SHA256 verification. **UPDATE REQUIRED (PRD v0.2.8+):** The release tarball must now also include the XDG autostart `.desktop` (F17, PACKAGING.md §4/§4.7) and the AUR `package()` must install it to `/etc/xdg/autostart/`. New subtask P1.M1.T1.S3 tracks this.

subtasks.title: Create AUR-adapted PKGBUILD for binary releases
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The existing PKGBUILD at packaging/linux/arch/PKGBUILD builds from source via `cargo build --release` and installs from `target/release/`. It links `-lhidapi-hidraw`. The AUR `-bin` package must instead download the GitHub release tarball `qmkonnect-${pkgver}-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (created by the CI linux-binary job) which contains `qmkonnect`, `qmkonnect-hid-id`, `udev/69-qmkonnect-rawhid.rules`, and `systemd/qmkonnect.service.template`. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §1 for AUR-specific requirements.
2. INPUT: The CI linux-binary job (release.yml lines ~155-185) stages the tarball with this layout: `qmkonnect-{ver}-linux-x86_64/{qmkonnect,qmkonnect-hid-id,udev/69-qmkonnect-rawhid.rules,systemd/qmkonnect.service.template}`. The GitHub release URL pattern is `https://github.com/dabstractor/qmkonnect/releases/download/v${pkgver}/qmkonnect-${pkgver}-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`.
3. LOGIC: Create `packaging/linux/aur/PKGBUILD` with: `pkgname=qmkonnect-bin`, `source=()` pointing at the GitHub release tarball URL, `sha256sums` placeholder (`SKIP` or computed), `arch=('x86_64')`, same `depends`/`install`/`backup`/`options` as the source PKGBUILD. The `package()` function extracts the pre-built binaries and installs them to the same paths (`/usr/bin/qmkonnect`, `/usr/lib/udev/qmkonnect-hid-id`, `/usr/lib/udev/rules.d/69-qmkonnect-rawhid.rules`, `/usr/lib/systemd/user/qmkonnect.service.template`). No `build()` function needed (binary package). Reuse the existing `qmkonnect.install` pacman hooks file (copy or symlink).
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/linux/aur/PKGBUILD` ready for AUR publication.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update packaging/linux/aur/README.md (create if absent) documenting the AUR package, its `-bin` suffix convention, and how to install (`yay -S qmkonnect-bin` or equivalent). This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Create .SRCINFO + AUR repo publication infrastructure
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: AUR packages require a `.SRCINFO` file (generated by `makepkg --printsrcinfo > .SRCINFO`) alongside the PKGBUILD. The AUR repo is a git remote at `aur@aur.archlinux.org/qmkonnect-bin.git` containing only PKGBUILD + .SRCINFO + .install. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §1.
2. INPUT: `packaging/linux/aur/PKGBUILD` from P1.M1.T1.S1.

Create `packaging/linux/aur/publish.sh` — a script that: (a) generates .SRCINFO via `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, (b) commits PKGBUILD + .SRCINFO + qmkonnect.install, (c) pushes to the AUR git remote. The script takes the version as an argument and patches `pkgver` in PKGBUILD before generating .SRCINFO. Document that an SSH deploy key for the AUR account must be configured.
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/linux/aur/.SRCINFO`, `packaging/linux/aur/publish.sh`, ready for CI integration in P1.M5.T1.S1.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add instructions in packaging/linux/aur/README.md for manual AUR publication (the publish.sh script usage). This rides WITH the work.

tasks.title: Nix Flake
tasks.description: Create a Nix flake (`flake.nix` + `flake.lock`) at the repo root that builds QMKonnect from source using `rustPlatform.buildRustPackage`, with proper Linux build dependencies (gtk3, hidapi, libxdo, systemd) and udev/systemd integration. **UPDATE REQUIRED (PRD v0.2.8+):** The flake `postInstall` must now also ship the XDG autostart `.desktop` (F17, PACKAGING.md §4.5/§4.7). New subtask P1.M1.T2.S3 tracks this.

subtasks.title: Create flake.nix with buildRustPackage + Linux deps
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The PRD says Nix 'builds from source' (§12). The project uses `RUSTFLAGS='-C link-arg=-lhidapi-hidraw'` (PKGBUILD build() and PACKAGING §2). Linux build deps from Cargo.toml `[target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")']`: hyprland (optional), libxdo, tempfile, libc, ksni (optional), gtk (optional). System libs: `libgtk-3-dev libglib2.0-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev libx11-dev libxcb1-dev libxdo-dev libhidapi-dev libudev-dev` (from CI linux-binary job). MSRV 1.88. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §5.
2. INPUT: `Cargo.toml` (for crate metadata, `cargoHash`), `Cargo.lock` (for reproducible builds), `.cargo/config.toml` (Windows CRT-static, not needed for Linux but flake should be cross-platform aware).
3. LOGIC: Create `flake.nix` at repo root with: `inputs.nixpkgs` (unstable or stable), `outputs = { self, nixpkgs, ... }:` producing `packages.{x86_64-linux,aarch64-linux}.qmkonnect` and `packages.{x86_64-linux,aarch64-linux}.default`. Use `rustPlatform.buildRustPackage` with `cargoHash` (or `cargoLock.lockFile`), `nativeBuildInputs = [ pkg-config ]`, `buildInputs = [ gtk3 glib libayatana-appindicator libx11 libxcb xdotool hidapi libusb systemd ]`, and `RUSTFLAGS = "-C link-arg=-lhidapi-hidraw"`. Also build the `qmkonnect-hid-id` binary (it's a separate bin target in the same crate, so it builds automatically). Add `devShells.default` for `nix develop`. Generate `flake.lock` via `nix flake lock`.
4. OUTPUT: `flake.nix` + `flake.lock` at repo root. Users can `nix run github:dabstractor/qmkonnect` or `nix build`.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Create packaging/nix/README.md documenting installation (`nix profile install github:dabstractor/qmkonnect`), the post-install udev/systemd steps (Nix can't install udev rules system-wide), and the `nix develop` shell. This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Add udev rule + hid-id + systemd integration to Nix package
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The udev rule (`packaging/linux/udev/69-qmkonnect-rawhid.rules`) references `/usr/lib/udev/qmkonnect-hid-id` (the helper binary). The systemd service template (`packaging/linux/systemd/qmkonnect.service.template`) has `ExecStart=/usr/bin/qmkonnect` and `BindsTo=dev-qmkonnect_device.device`. On NixOS, the system-level udev rule and systemd service need NixOS module integration. On non-NixOS distros using Nix, users install the binary manually and must set up udev/systemd themselves. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §5.
2. INPUT: `flake.nix` from P1.M1.T2.S1, `packaging/linux/udev/69-qmkonnect-rawhid.rules`, `packaging/linux/systemd/qmkonnect.service.template`, `src/bin/hid_id.rs`.
3. LOGIC: In `flake.nix`, add a `postInstall` phase to the `buildRustPackage` that: (a) copies the udev helper `qmkonnect-hid-id` to `$out/lib/udev/`, (b) copies the udev rule to `$out/lib/udev/rules.d/`, (c) copies the systemd template to `$out/lib/systemd/user/`. Additionally create a `nixosModule` output in the flake (a NixOS module that: registers the udev rule via `services.udev.packages`, enables the systemd user service, and adds the user to the `input` group). The module is optional — non-NixOS users just use the binary package and set up udev manually.
4. OUTPUT: Updated `flake.nix` with `postInstall` + `nixosModules.default` output. The package ships all four files (qmkonnect, qmkonnect-hid-id, udev rule, service template).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update packaging/nix/README.md with NixOS module usage (`configuration.nix`: `inputs.qmkonnect.nixosModules.default`) and non-NixOS manual udev setup steps. This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Update Nix flake postInstall to ship XDG autostart .desktop (F17)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The updated PRD (F17, PACKAGING.md §4.5/§4.7) requires the XDG autostart `.desktop` to ship in every Linux package. The existing Nix flake (P1.M1.T2.S2, Complete) has a `postInstall` that copies the binary, hid-id helper, udev rule, and systemd template — it does not yet copy the `.desktop`.
2. INPUT: `packaging/linux/xdg/qmkonnect.desktop` (created by P2.M6.T1.S1), `flake.nix` (from P1.M1.T2.S2).
3. LOGIC: In `flake.nix`'s `postInstall`, add a step to copy the `.desktop` file to `$out/etc/xdg/autostart/qmkonnect.desktop`. The NixOS module already uses systemd (primary); the `.desktop` is a belt-and-suspenders for non-NixOS/manual Nix installs. Regenerate `flake.lock` if inputs change.
4. OUTPUT: Updated `flake.nix` postInstall.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update packaging/nix/README.md noting the `.desktop` is included.

milestones.title: Cross-Platform Version Managers (mise + asdf)
milestones.description: Create an asdf plugin that mise can also use directly (mise is asdf-compatible). The plugin downloads the appropriate pre-built release binary for the user's OS/arch and installs it into the version manager's prefix. This covers both mise and asdf from a single plugin.

tasks.title: asdf Plugin (compatible with mise)
tasks.description: Create the asdf plugin shell scripts (bin/install, bin/list-all, bin/download) and document mise compatibility. The plugin lives in a separate repo `dabstractor/asdf-qmkonnect` but the scripts are staged in `packaging/asdf/` in this repo for CI to publish.

subtasks.title: Create asdf plugin scripts (install, list-all, download)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: asdf plugins are shell-script based, living in a separate repo named `asdf-{toolname}`. The three required scripts are: `bin/list-all` (prints available versions), `bin/download` (fetches the release artifact for a given version + OS/arch), `bin/install` (extracts to `$ASDF_INSTALL_PATH`). Release artifacts per platform: macOS=`QMKonnect-{ver}-macos.dmg` (need to extract .app from DMG), Windows=`QMKonnect-{ver}-windows-x64.exe`, Linux=`qmkonnect-{ver}-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (contains qmkonnect + qmkonnect-hid-id + udev + systemd). mise is fully asdf-compatible: `mise plugin add qmkonnet https://github.com/dabstractor/asdf-qmkonnect` works without any plugin changes. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §6-7.
2. INPUT: GitHub Releases API: `https://api.github.com/repos/dabstractor/qmkonnect/releases` for version listing. Release artifact naming patterns (from CI release.yml): macOS DMG, Windows exe, Linux tarball.
3. LOGIC: Create `packaging/asdf/bin/list-all` — scrapes GitHub API for tags, prints space-separated versions. Create `packaging/asdf/bin/download` — maps `uname -s`/`uname -m` to artifact name, downloads via `curl`, validates SHA256 if sidecar exists. Create `packaging/asdf/bin/install` — extracts the platform-appropriate artifact to `$ASDF_INSTALL_PATH/bin/` (Linux: tar extract; macOS: mount DMG + copy qmkonnect binary from the .app bundle; note: the raw binary works for CLI but not menu-bar without the bundle context — document this caveat). Also create `packaging/asdf/lib/utils.bash` for shared helper functions.
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/asdf/bin/{list-all,download,install}`, `packaging/asdf/lib/utils.bash`.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Create packaging/asdf/README.md (the plugin repo README) documenting: asdf setup (`asdf plugin add qmkonnect https://github.com/dabstractor/asdf-qmkonnect`, `asdf install qmkonnect latest`, `asdf global qmkonnect latest`), mise setup (`mise plugin add qmkonnect ...`, `mise install qmkonnect@latest`), and the macOS caveat that the raw binary lacks bundle context for the menu-bar icon. This rides WITH the work.

1. RESEARCH NOTE: asdf plugins need a `.tool-versions` example and optionally a `mise.toml` for mise-native support. While mise can use asdf plugins directly, a `mise.toml` in the plugin repo enables mise-specific features. The plugin also needs a `CHANGELOG.md` and a GitHub Actions workflow for testing. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §6-7.

3. LOGIC: Create `packaging/asdf/.tool-versions` example (`qmkonnect 0.2.8`). Create `packaging/asdf/mise.toml` with `[tools]` section documenting the asdf-compat path. backlog.title: F16/F17 — Cross-DE Linux Window Monitor + Universal Autostart
backlog.description: PRD UPDATE (v0.2.8+): Two entirely new top-level features. F16 — a runtime-selected multi-backend Linux window monitor (foreign-toplevel Wayland -> GNOME Shell extension -> Hyprland IPC -> AT-SPI -> X11) so one binary works on GNOME, KDE Plasma, COSMIC, Hyprland, Sway, Niri, wlroots, and the X11 DE tail. F17 — universal XDG autostart `.desktop` alongside the systemd user service for login-autostart on systemd and non-systemd distros (MX/Artix/Void/Gentoo). This phase spans new source modules (`src/platforms/{wayland_ft,gnome,atspi}.rs`), a `select_linux_backend` dispatcher, a GNOME Shell extension artifact (`packaging/gnome-shell-extension/`), new Cargo features (`wayland`/`gnome`/`atspi`), config schema additions (`[linux]` table), and the hidapi-link-per-distro nuance (ARCHITECTURE.md invariant 12). Fully specified in PLATFORMS.md §6-§10, ARCHITECTURE.md §3/§6/§9, CONFIG.md §1/§1.3, LINUX.md §6.3, PACKAGING.md §2/§4/§7/§9.

tasks.title: select_linux_backend runtime dispatcher
tasks.description: Implement `select_linux_backend(verbose) -> Result<Box<dyn WindowMonitor>, Box<dyn Error>>` (in `src/platforms/mod.rs` or `linux.rs`) that probes each compiled-in backend for availability in priority order (foreign-toplevel -> GNOME -> Hyprland -> AT-SPI -> X11) and returns the first present one. Replaces the old compile-time `cfg(feature="hyprland")` either/or with runtime selection so one binary works across all desktops.

subtasks.title: Implement select_linux_backend with priority probing + verbose logging + no-backend fallback
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The updated PLATFORMS.md §6 defines `select_linux_backend` as the runtime selector with this priority order: (1) foreign-toplevel Wayland [feature `wayland`] — gate: `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY` resolvable AND compositor advertises `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1`; (2) GNOME Shell extension [feature `gnome`] — gate: D-Bus name `io.mulletware.QMKonnect` owned; (3) Hyprland IPC [feature `hyprland`] — gate: `$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` + live socket; (4) AT-SPI [feature `atspi`] — gate: a11y bus reachable; (5) X11 [always on Linux] — gate: `$DISPLAY` set AND `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset AND xprop present. ARCHITECTURE.md §2.2 says `create_monitor` delegates to `select_linux_backend`. The `[linux] backend` config can override auto selection. The no-backend fallback (e.g. GNOME-Wayland without extension + a11y off) returns Err but the runner still starts tray/device-status/HID pipeline; on GNOME a one-shot notify-send fires (PLATFORMS.md §8.4).
2. INPUT: `src/platforms/mod.rs` (create_monitor + WindowMonitor trait), the per-backend availability probes (each backend's T1). This subtask implements the dispatcher and the probe stubs; backends are wired in P2.M2-P2.M5.
3. LOGIC: (a) In `src/platforms/mod.rs`/`linux.rs`, add `select_linux_backend(verbose)` that iterates the priority list, calls each backend's availability probe, returns the first `Ok`. (b) Each probe is a cheap check (env var + D-Bus name ownership + socket existence). (c) Honor `[linux] backend` config override (forced backend that's unavailable errors loudly with every probe result). (d) Verbose mode prints each candidate, probe result, and chosen backend. (e) On total failure (all probes fail), return Err; the runner (`runners/linux.rs`) handles it by still starting the tray/device pipeline and emitting no window events; GNOME first-run notification fires here. (f) Wire `create_monitor` to call `select_linux_backend` on Linux. Invariant 11: NEVER select X11 under a Wayland compositor (X11 gate requires `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset).
4. OUTPUT: `select_linux_backend` in `src/platforms/{mod,linux}.rs`, `create_monitor` updated, runner handles the no-backend Err gracefully.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Backend selection is logged verbosely; document the priority order + `[linux] backend` override in docs.

milestones.description: The single highest-leverage backend: one Wayland client speaking the foreign-toplevel protocols covers every wlroots-derived compositor plus KDE Plasma and COSMIC (Hyprland, Sway, Niri, River, Labwc, Wayfire, KDE Plasma 6/KWin, COSMIC/Smithay). Uses `wlr-foreign-toplevel-management-v1` for activation/focus state (the load-bearing protocol) and `ext-foreign-toplevel-list-v1` for cross-checking app_ids and populating the window-info dialog.

tasks.title: Implement wayland_ft.rs backend
tasks.description: Create `src/platforms/wayland_ft.rs` (feature `wayland`) implementing WindowMonitor via smithay-client-toolkit's foreign-toplevel handler. spawn-and-return `start()` (dedicated EventQueue dispatch thread), per-toplevel tracking (app_id/title/state), empty-workspace -> empty WindowInfo, reconnect backoff, and list_foreground_windows() snapshot.

subtasks.title: Core wayland_ft.rs: wlr focus tracking + ext cross-check + spawn-and-return + reconnect
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: PLATFORMS.md §7 specifies: bind `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` (the focus source — the `state` event's `activated` flag is how we know which toplevel is focused) and `ext-foreign-toplevel-list-v1` (upstream successor; lists app_id/title/identifier but does NOT report activation — use only to populate list_foreground_windows and cross-check app_ids). Coverage: Hyprland, Sway, Niri, River, Labwc, Wayfire, KDE Plasma 6 (KWin), COSMIC; GNOME (Mutter) implements neither -> falls through to P2.M3. `app_class` = the toplevel's `app_id` (`.desktop` basename, reverse-DNS passed through verbatim). Empty workspace (no toplevel carries `activated`) -> WindowInfo{app_class:"",title:""} (deactivates layers). Reconnect backoff reuses Hyprland constants (INITIAL_RECONNECT_MS=100, MAX=10_000, x3, reset after 5s stable). smithay-client-toolkit provides ForeignToplevelManager/ForeignToplevelHandler. ARCHITECTURE.md §3/§6: start() SPAWNS the dispatch thread and RETURNS (unlike Hyprland blocking); monitor owns Arc<Mutex<Option<(String,String)>>> last-state cell; runner parks main.
2. INPUT: `Cargo.toml` (smithay-client-toolkit dep from P2.M1.T2.S2), `src/platforms/mod.rs` (WindowMonitor trait, select_linux_backend probe stub from P2.M1.T1.S1).
3. LOGIC: (a) Implement a WaylandFtMonitor struct implementing WindowMonitor. (b) `start()`: connect wl_display, bind wlr-foreign-toplevel-manager (focus) + ext-foreign-toplevel-list (cross-check) if present, spawn a thread running the EventQueue dispatch loop, return immediately. (c) Per-toplevel tracking: on `toplevel` event create handle; cache app_id/title/state bitmask; update on title/app_id/state events; remove on closed; commit on done. After each done, recompute the toplevel whose state includes `activated`; if it differs from last reported (app_class,title), emit notify_qmk. (d) Empty workspace -> empty WindowInfo. (e) `stop()`: drop the queue/thread. (f) Reconnect with backoff on wl_display error. (g) `list_foreground_windows()`: snapshot all tracked toplevels as (app_id,title), activated first. (h) Availability probe for select_linux_backend: $WAYLAND_DISPLAY resolvable AND compositor advertises wlr global.
4. OUTPUT: `src/platforms/wayland_ft.rs` (feature `wayland`), wired into select_linux_backend as priority #1.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Document the protocol coverage table in PLATFORMS.md §7.2 is the reference; update docs for the new backend.

milestones.title: GNOME Backend (Shell Extension + D-Bus Client)
milestones.description: GNOME (Mutter) implements neither foreign-toplevel protocol and exposes no client API for the active window, so the active window is read inside `gnome-shell` by a small extension and republished over the session D-Bus, where the desktop app subscribes. Two deliverables: the `qmkonnect@mulletware` GNOME Shell extension (separate artifact) and `src/platforms/gnome.rs` (the D-Bus client backend).

tasks.title: GNOME Shell extension (packaging/gnome-shell-extension/)
tasks.description: Create the `qmkonnect@mulletware` GNOME Shell extension (GJS, GNOME Shell 45+) that runs in the gnome-shell process, reads `global.display.focus_window`, and republishes `(app_class, title)` over the session D-Bus. This is a SEPARATE artifact from the app binary (the app cannot load it).

subtasks.title: Create extension.js + metadata.json + D-Bus export
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: PLATFORMS.md §8.1-§8.2 + PACKAGING.md §7 specify the D-Bus contract: well-known name `io.mulletware.QMKonnect` (owned <=> extension installed & enabled), object path `/io/mulletware/QMKonnect`, interface `io.mulletware.QMKonnect.WindowMonitor` with method `GetActiveWindow() -> (s app_class, s title)`, signal `ActiveWindowChanged(s app_class, s title)`, properties AppClass/Title. `app_class` = `MetaWindow.get_wm_class()` (the WM_CLASS class — parity with X11). title = `MetaWindow.get_title()`. GJS, GNOME Shell 45+ APIs. metadata.json: uuid=`qmkonnect@mulletware`, shell-version covering supported GNOME line (e.g. ['45','46','47','48','49','50']), version=QMKonnect release.
2. INPUT: PLATFORMS.md §8.2 (enable/disable/_onFocus logic), PACKAGING.md §7 (build/zip/distribution).

(b) Create `packaging/gnome-shell-extension/extension.js`: `enable()` acquires the D-Bus name, exports the object/interface on the session bus, connects `global.display.connect('notify::focus-window', ...)`, emits initial state; `_onFocus()` reads `global.display.focus_window` -> `[w.get_wm_class() ?? '', w.get_title() ?? '']` (or ['',''] if null), dedups against last-emitted, emits `ActiveWindowChanged`; `disable()` disconnects, releases name, unexports. Fallbacks: get_wm_class() may be null -> empty class. (c) Optional `prefs.js`, `stylesheet.css`.
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/gnome-shell-extension/{metadata.json,extension.js}` (+ optional prefs.js/stylesheet.css).

tasks.title: GNOME D-Bus client backend (src/platforms/gnome.rs)
tasks.description: Create `src/platforms/gnome.rs` (feature `gnome`) — the desktop-side zbus D-Bus client that subscribes to the extension's `ActiveWindowChanged` signal, drift-polls `GetActiveWindow`, watches NameOwnerChanged, and fires a first-run notification when the extension isn't installed.

subtasks.title: Implement gnome.rs: zbus subscription + drift poll + NameOwnerChanged + first-run notification
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: PLATFORMS.md §8.3 specifies: zbus session connection; subscribe to `ActiveWindowChanged` -> dedup -> notify_qmk. Drift-correcting poll thread (default 1000ms, hot-config via `[linux] gnome_poll_interval_ms`) calls GetActiveWindow and dedups. NameOwnerChanged watch: if the extension is toggled mid-session, re-acquire initial state from GetActiveWindow; if the name goes away, report empty and apply the no-backend posture. ARCHITECTURE.md §3/§6: monitor runs on a background zbus thread + a 1000ms drift-poll thread; ksni owns its D-Bus thread; runner parks main. Availability probe for select_linux_backend: the D-Bus well-known name `io.mulletware.QMKonnect` is owned on the session bus.
2. INPUT: `Cargo.toml` (zbus dep from P2.M1.T2.S2), the D-Bus contract from P2.M3.T1.S1, `[linux] gnome_poll_interval_ms` config from P2.M1.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: (a) Implement a GnomeMonitor struct implementing WindowMonitor. (b) `start()`: connect zbus session; subscribe to ActiveWindowChanged signal; spawn a background signal-listener thread; spawn the 1000ms (hot-config) drift-poll thread calling GetActiveWindow + dedup; install a NameOwnerChanged watch for the extension name. (c) On signal/poll -> dedup -> notify_qmk. (d) Empty window (focus_window null) -> empty WindowInfo. (e) Availability probe: check the session bus for `io.mulletware.QMKonnect` ownership. (f) `list_foreground_windows()`: call GetActiveWindow (single window).
4. OUTPUT: `src/platforms/gnome.rs` (feature `gnome`), wired into select_linux_backend as priority #2.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Document the backend + the extension dependency in docs.

subtasks.title: First-run GNOME notification when extension missing
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: PLATFORMS.md §8.4 specifies: if the session is GNOME (`$XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` contains `GNOME`) AND the extension name is not owned at startup, fire a ONE-SHOT desktop notification (via `platforms::notify`/notify-send): 'QMKonnect needs the GNOME Shell extension for window detection — install it from extensions.gnome.org (see docs).' The daemon keeps running (tray + device status); the AT-SPI backend (P2.M4) may run meanwhile as a best-effort interim. Fires at most once per launch.
2. INPUT: `src/platforms/gnome.rs` (from P2.M3.T2.S1), the notify-send helper used elsewhere.
3. LOGIC: At startup (in start() or the runner), if `$XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` contains GNOME and the `io.mulletware.QMKonnect` name is not owned, fire a one-shot notify-send notification with a link to docs. Guard with a static AtomicBool so it fires at most once per process.
4. OUTPUT: One-shot GNOME notification in gnome.rs/runner.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] The notification message links to docs; ensure docs/qmk-integration.md covers the extension.

milestones.title: AT-SPI Fallback Backend (src/platforms/atspi.rs)
milestones.description: The last-ditch backend for any compositor with accessibility enabled — primarily a GNOME fallback when the extension isn't installed and an emergency path elsewhere. Best-effort, not primary. Uses the `atspi` crate (zbus to the a11y bus).

tasks.title: Implement atspi.rs backend
tasks.description: Create `src/platforms/atspi.rs` (feature `atspi`) — subscribe to `object:state-changed:focused` a11y events, track the focused accessible, report its application Name as app_class and its Name as title, with a 1000ms poll fallback. Documented limitations (readable name != WM_CLASS, Electron/sandboxed apps inconsistent, a11y often off by default).

subtasks.title: Core atspi.rs: a11y-bus event subscription + 1000ms poll + best-effort limitations
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: PLATFORMS.md §9 specifies: crate `atspi` (zbus to a11y bus). Subscribe to `object:state-changed:focused` events; track the focused accessible. `app_class` = the focused accessible's application `Name` (org.a11y.atspi.Application -> Name — the readable name, UNRELIABLE); `title` = the focused accessible's `Name`. Poll fallback: every 1000ms query the a11y registry's focused object and dedup. Availability: the a11y bus is present (org.a11y.Bus owned or $ATSPI_BUS_ADDRESS). Most distros ship a11y OFF until the user enables 'Assistive Technology / Screen Reader' — document that. Known limitations: app_class is readable name not WM_CLASS (fine for Firefox, inconsistent for Electron/sandboxed); titles vary (focused accessible not toplevel); apps without a11y bridge are invisible.
2. INPUT: `Cargo.toml` (atspi dep from P2.M1.T2.S2), `src/platforms/mod.rs` (select_linux_backend probe).
3. LOGIC: (a) Implement an AtspiMonitor struct implementing WindowMonitor. (b) `start()`: connect to the a11y bus; subscribe to object:state-changed:focused on a background thread; spawn a 1000ms poll thread querying the focused object. (c) On event/poll -> dedup -> notify_qmk. (d) Availability probe: org.a11y.Bus owned or $ATSPI_BUS_ADDRESS set. (e) `list_foreground_windows()`: best-effort single focused accessible. (f) Document the limitations clearly (README/docs).
4. OUTPUT: `src/platforms/atspi.rs` (feature `atspi`), wired into select_linux_backend as priority #4.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Document the best-effort nature + the a11y-enable requirement in docs/troubleshooting.md.

subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: PLATFORMS.md §10 says X11 is compiled in on every Linux build (no feature flag) and selected only for genuine X11 sessions. subtasks.title: Create packaging/linux/xdg/qmkonnect.desktop + ship in all Linux packages
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The updated LINUX.md §6.3 + PACKAGING.md §4.7 specify an XDG autostart entry at `/etc/xdg/autostart/qmkonnect.desktop`. Every DE session manager honors `~/.config/autostart/` and `/etc/xdg/autostart/`, so this starts the daemon at LOGIN on every desktop — systemd or not. Contents: Type=Application, Name=QMKonnect, Comment, Exec=qmkonnect, Icon=input-keyboard, Terminal=false, X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=true, Categories=Utility;, NoDisplay=true (autostart-only — not in app menus). Trade-off vs the service: login-only start, loses the systemd BindsTo plug/unplug lifecycle; on systemd distros the service remains primary; the .desktop is redundant-but-harmless (single-instance story is owned by the tray/runner, not the launcher). The user disables it by copying to ~/.config/autostart/ with Hidden=true. PACKAGING.md §4 lists it in the shared artifact table (7th file).
2. INPUT: PACKAGING.md §4.7 (exact .desktop contents), LINUX.md §6.3.
3. LOGIC: (a) Create `packaging/linux/xdg/qmkonnect.desktop` with the exact contents from PACKAGING.md §4.7. (b) The CI linux-binary tarball (release.yml) must include it. (c) Every package installs it to `/etc/xdg/autostart/`: Arch source PKGBUILD (`packaging/linux/arch/PKGBUILD`), AUR `-bin` (P1.M1.T1.S3), Nix (P1.M1.T2.S3), .deb (P1.M7.T1.S1), .rpm (P1.M7.T2.S1). (d) Document that on systemd distros the service is primary and the .desktop is belt-and-suspenders; on non-systemd it's load-bearing.
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/linux/xdg/qmkonnect.desktop` + integration into the CI tarball + all package install paths.
